manifest.title: Existing CKA Transfer Baseline Audit
manifest.description: Technical audit of the pre-correction eight-image transfer baseline and the corrective baseline now running.

blocks.body:
## Technical summary

The weak intra-family results cannot yet be treated as a failure of the proposed method. The historical implementation mixed representation levels: Qwen and InternVL attack CKA used pre-projector vision features, while their classification loss and Gemma CKA used language-model input tokens. Among 85 historical trials that passed both proxy 8/8 gates and had eight clean-valid target images, higher recorded reference-CKA gain was not associated with higher transfer (pooled Spearman -0.227). This is a diagnostic result, not an inference, because trials reuse images and mix pairs and objectives. The existing baseline has therefore been corrected before any new attack method is introduced.

## Historical results do not validate the intended CKA mechanism

Only Qwen-4B to Qwen-2B reached the requested 4/8 in any eligible historical trial. InternVL-4B to 2B peaked at 2/8 and Gemma-E4B to E2B at 1/8. Within those pairs, the descriptive rank association between reference-CKA gain and target hits was non-positive, so simply increasing the old CKA term is not supported by these runs.

## Scope and metric definitions

An eligible trial is complete, has closed-set proxy success 8/8, proxy free-generation success 8/8, and a target clean-valid denominator of 8. `Target hits` count adversarial target outputs equal to class 7 only among images whose clean target output equals source class 8. `Reference CKA gain` is the change from clean-reference CKA to adversarial-reference CKA recorded by the historical attack tap. The audit excludes the newly launched projected-token baseline until it finishes.

## The primary problem was implementation alignment, not one lambda value

The attack path, evaluation path, and analysis path were traced independently. Four implementation defects could materially invalidate or contaminate the conclusion; three are now corrected and one requires a held-out experimental result.

## Audit method and validation

The review followed the full data path: canonical 224 PNG, differentiable native preprocessing, proxy 10-way scoring, visual-token extraction, per-image token CKA, momentum PGD, PNG round-trip gate, and target generation. Historical summaries were filtered with a reproducible script. The corrected implementation uses each generative model's `get_image_features(...).pooler_output`, the same projected visual soft tokens consumed by its language model. Formal smoke and scaled attacks now use the full configured step budget. The test suite passes 70 tests with 3 intentional smoke skips.

## Limitations and robustness boundaries

The historical correlations are not independent estimates: the same eight images appear in many trials, configurations differ, and pair identity strongly confounds pooled results. Token-level linear CKA is also rotation-invariant and centers across spatial tokens, so it can improve token-geometry similarity without necessarily moving the class-semantic direction. That method-level concern remains unresolved until the layer-correct baseline is evaluated. Model-similarity global/local CKA has not yet produced an analysis CSV, so the proxy-selector hypothesis itself is not yet tested.

## Recommended next steps

1. Finish the 15-trial projected-token baseline for P20, P21, and P22, including the lambda-zero control and the declared lambda/alpha combinations.
2. Require 8/8 proxy closed-set and free-generation success, then judge transfer on disjoint target evaluation.
3. Do not promote any configuration to 50 images until all three large-to-small intra-family pairs are reviewed and the selected configuration is confirmed on held-out images.
4. Only if the corrected baseline still fails should a new branch introduce a different transfer method such as input diversity, translation-invariant gradients, or prompt ensembles.

## Further questions

Does projected-token CKA improve transfer beyond the lambda-zero classification control? Does a target-attraction-only CKA objective outperform the current source-repulsion plus target-attraction form? After a fixed attack is selected without target-image reuse, do global and local proxy-target CKA predict held-out TASR?
